title: Extended Warranties: The Very Profitable Consumer Trap!
summary: An audio-equipment dealer warns that extended warranties aren't regulated insurance, often overlap with existing coverage, and should be read carefully before buying.

assertions.quote: Extended warranty companies have none of that. There is no state regulation um uh on extended warranties.

verdicts.note: Vehicle/appliance service contracts are regulated in many states under service-contract statutes, but with lighter reserve requirements than true insurance, so 'none' overstates it.

NCLC notes that unlike insurance (regulated, with agents earning fixed commissions and minimum loss ratios as low as 40% even for the least-regulated insurance products), add-on products like service contracts are unregulated and show far lower effective loss ratios.

assertions.quote: Because as I said, much of that money goes right to the bottom line of the company.
Many times these extended warranties run coterminously or the same time as the manufacturer's warranty on the product.
also be careful because many charge card companies um essentially have a sort of extended warranty built into their system
some companies go so far as to hire and fire based upon their ability to get extended warranties

verdicts.note: Extended warranties are widely reported as high-margin products with sales quotas or incentive pay tied to attachment rates in retail and auto finance.

assertions.quote: many extended warranties on automobiles don't cover emission systems because failures are usually very expensive
Their advice is simply buy a better product because it's built better and be done with it.
